Article Title: Cold medicines for under-4s face curbs over safety concerns
Article Text:
File photo: A medicine shop

NEW DELHI: Parents of children below four years will now have to be more cautious about giving them combination medicines for cold symptoms, with the Centre restricting the manufacture, sale and distribution of all fixed-dose combinations (FDCs) containing chlorpheniramine maleate and phenylephrine hydrochloride.The government has said these combinations may pose risks to children below four and that safer alternatives are available. Manufacturers have been ordered to carry a prominent warning on the drug label, package insert and promotional material stating: “Fixed Dose Combination shall not be used in children below four years of age.”Dr Rommel Tickoo, senior director, internal medicine, Max hospital, said, “In children below four years, combination cold medicines containing chlorpheniramine and phenylephrine can cause excessive drowsiness or agitation, rapid heartbeat and, in some cases, serious adverse effects. Since these medicines offer limited benefit for a common cold, parents should prefer safer measures such as saline nasal drops, adequate fluids and honey for children above one year. ”The move is the latest step in a regulatory review that dates back to 2023, when concerns were raised over the use of the combination in young children. The issue was re-examined in 2024 with paediatricians, with DTAB recommending that the warning apply to all formulations.The Centre subsequently imposed restrictions in April 2025, and DTAB revisited the matter in February 2026, agreeing to extend the restriction to all formulations.The latest notification now covers all such formulations, including those manufactured or imported and marketed in India.The decision follows recommendations of an Expert Committee constituted by the Health Ministry and the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB). DTAB, at its February 16, 2026 meeting, agreed that the formulations should not be used in children below four.Issued under Section 26A of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, the notification came into force upon publication in the Official Gazette.
Article Summary: The government has said these combinations may pose risks to children below four. Manufacturers have been ordered to carry a prominent warning on the drug label, package insert and promotional material. The move is the latest step in a regulatory review that dates back to 2023.

Article Title: No work, no study, no training: 8.7 crore Indian youth caught in a career gap
Article Text:
8.7 crore Indian youth caught in a career limbo

Cost remains a barrier

Career mismatch

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

More than 8 crore Indian youth are caught in a difficult spot — with no job, no education and no training.According to a Niti Aayog report, an estimated 8.7 crore Indians aged 15 to 29 fall into this category. The figure, based on the 78th round of the National Sample Survey conducted in 2021, was highlighted in Niti Aayog's report Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat@2047.It called for subsidised training programmes to help young people move towards self-employment and develop skills that match local demand and emerging sectors.The report divided India's workforce and learners into five broad groups: those in schooling, tertiary education, formal and informal work, not in education, employment and training (NEET) youth, and women. It said that young people outside education, employment and training face a particular financial hurdle as they have no income while already having spent on their earlier education."NEET youth are constrained by the absence of income and the sunk cost of prior education. Students often cannot layer paid skilling onto existing financial commitments," it said.For students from low-income households, adding a paid skilling course to the cost of college and, in many cases, private tuition can be difficult to afford, the report said.This can leave young people with limited room to invest in additional training alongside a conventional degree.The report said some graduates subsequently take up formal employment simply to secure an income and support their families, even when the available job is low-paying. Others find it difficult to make the transition from education to employment and eventually become NEET."As a result, many students choose to get themselves a formal job/income source after graduation to support their families and often end up taking whatever brings in some stable income even if that is low-paying; others, however, struggle to transition into work and become NEET," the Aayog said.The gap between having a degree and finding the right job remains stark, with only 8.25 per cent of graduates employed in roles that match their qualifications. The report said limited exposure to practical learning and industry-aligned training continues to affect employability, even among formally educated youth.The Aayog said that NEET youth and women need affordable or subsidised training options, backed by dedicated financial support where financial constraints are most binding. It also emphasised the importance of allowing people to learn while earning."For the workforce and NEET youth, the need shifts towards mid-career reskilling, self-employment pathways, and learning options aligned to local demand and emerging sectors," the Aayog said in the report.The report said India's Viksit Bharat 2047 ambition rests on enabling citizens to keep learning, earning and progressing, making skilling a key part of that effort.Since 2014-15, more than 7.67 crore people have been trained, the Aayog added.
Article Summary: 8.7 crore indian youth caught in a career limbo with no job, no education and no training. Niti aayog report: an estimated 8.7 lakh indians aged 15 to 29 fall into this category. Report called for subsidised training programmes to help young people move towards self-employment.

Article Title: Invoking Mahatma Gandhi, BJP to start nationwide Vande campaign

Month-long campaign for PM Modi's birthday

NEW DELHI: BJP cited Mahatma Gandhi's "we have fallen on evil days" lament over the opposition built up against Vande Mataram Saturday to set the stage for an intense political battle with Congress and the wider 'secular' class for their objections to the national song's full version by announcing a nationwide campaign.The campaign, approved at a meeting of the new office-bearers under party chief Nitin Nabin, will focus on the song's association with freedom struggle, opposition by Pakistan's founder M A Jinnah and other Muslim hardliners which led Congress to prune it and "communal pressure or narrow vote-bank considerations" driving the current protests against the national song.The meeting adopted a four-page resolution, accusing Congress of "bowing before the same politics of appeasement" to which it had yielded in 1937, enabling Jinnah-led Muslim League to impose communal demands even upon national symbols.BJP's decision to launch the 10-point campaign comes after Congress asserted that it will stick to its 1937 resolution that had adopted the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram to signal its defiance of the notification restoring its full version for all official events and Parliament passing a law making any insult to the song a penal offence. With Gen Z emerging as an axis of political mobilisation for its rivals after their successful protest over paper leaks, the campaign also seeks to target its pitch for Vande Mataram at the youth.PM Modi visited party headquarters to interact with the new team. Organisational meetings are all about new ideas aimed at strengthening the party and deepening connection with the people, he said.In its resolution, BJP marshalled comments of stalwarts like Gandhi and C Rajagopalachari to hit back at its rivals, who have accused it of stoking political divide over the song. It framed its campaign as a contest between the song's rich legacy versus a bid to truncate it to appease Muslim fundamentalists.It cited Gandhi's 1939 comments: "I associated the purest national spirit with it (Vande Mataram). It never occurred to me that it was a Hindu song or meant only for Hindus. Unfortunately, now we have fallen on evil days." Nabin accused Congress of sowing the same seeds of division that it did in 1937 by adopting a truncated version under the Muslim League's pressure.Several youth-centric programmes will be part of BJP's month-long campaign from Modi's birthday on Sept 17, with the annual "sewa" programme turning special this time as he will also be completing 25 years as head of a govt.
Article Summary: Campaign will focus on song's association with freedom struggle, opposition by pakistan's founder m a jinnah and other muslim hardliners. Meeting adopted a four-page resolution, accusing congress of "bowing before the same politics of appeasement" to which it had yielded in 1937.

Former Union minister and senior Congress leader P Chidambaram said on Friday that the party wants the existing allocation of Lok Sabha seats to be maintained for another 25 years, with no change to the current strength of 543 seats or Tamil Nadu’s 39 constituencies.Chidambaram added that the resolutions passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and the Congress Working Committee on delimitation reflected the same position.“The resolutions passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and the Congress Working Committee regarding the delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies reflect the same stance. There should be no change to the current Lok Sabha strength of 543 seats or Tamil Nadu’s allocation of 39 constituencies. The Congress party’s position is that the current seat allocations should be maintained for another 25 years,” Chidambaram said in a post on X.“It is gratifying that both the ruling party (TVK) and the principal opposition party (DMK) in Tamil Nadu support this stance,” he added.The development comes a day after Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay raised concerns over the proposed Delimitation Bill, 2026, warning that southern states could lose parliamentary representation if seats are redistributed primarily on the basis of population.Speaking at the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday, Vijay, who is also the council’s vice-chairman, sought an assurance from the Centre that states that had successfully stabilised their populations would not be penalised through a reduction in their parliamentary representation.He said the issue had assumed importance as the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census approaches its end."As the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census approaches its end and the Delimitation Bill, 2026, is considered, there is a genuine and shared concern across the Southern States that delimitation based predominantly on populations may diminish our collective voice in Parliament," he said.Vijay said southern states had successfully controlled population growth while making progress in human development and economic growth. He argued that these achievements should not lead to a reduction in their political representation.The Tamil Nadu Assembly had earlier passed a special resolution urging the Centre to permanently retain the Lok Sabha’s strength at 543 seats.The government-sponsored resolution also called for the 33 per cent reservation for women to be implemented in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections without delay, based on the existing strength of 543 seats.
Article Summary: Former union minister and senior congress leader p chidambaram said on friday that the party wants the existing allocation of lok sabha seats to be maintained for another 25 years. The development comes a day after tamil nadu chief minister joseph vijay raised concerns over the proposed delimitation bill, 2026.

Article Title: SC faults UP Gangsters Act, says it is prone to misuse
Article Text:
SC flags ‘serious flaws’ in UP Gangsters Act, warns of misuse against innocents

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Pointing out various flaws in Uttar Pradesh Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, Supreme Court on Thursday said the law is prone to misuse as there is no safeguard against vindictive and malicious action against innocents.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the special Act does not create any offence, which is the requirement of any penal law. "But for the definition clause, defining 'gang' and 'gangster', there is no offence insofar as the membership in the gang or acting in cohort with a gang, either singly or together," it said."The subject enactment, the UP Act not only permits detention for a period without anything more than the inclusion in a Gang Chart but also enables a trial and punishment on the basis of the very same Gang Chart, in addition to the pre-trial incarceration, but without an offence being created by the Act itself. It is akin to the English proverb: Give a dog a bad name and hang him," the bench said.Observing that the UP law fails to satisfy judicial conscience, SC said menace of criminal gangs is to be curbed, but the end does not justify the means, especially in enacting a penal law that interferes with liberty of citizens.The apex court was particularly concerned about two issues - "(1) the total absence of creation of a crime, which is mandatory in a penal statute and (2) the punishment being imposed on a status determined for a person, that too on the whim of the administrative officers and police personnel by preparation of a Gang Chart under the Rules, not specifically provided under the statute.""We cannot but observe, with respect, that there is always a tendency among the wisest of men to label a question; to which they find no answer or a difficult or unpalatable one, as foolish and the one who raised it, a fool," the bench said."We hence, endeavoured to find an answer to the two questions we have posed above, by posing it to the learned Counsel appearing for the State. We did so, at the risk of being called foolhardy and our only solace is that the very same questions were raised before the full bench of the Allahabad high court, at that juncture, but by wise men, eminent lawyers of considerable repute," it said.SC said the counsel appearing for the state neither could give an answer at the time of arguments nor attempted to do so in the written submissions placed before the court.The SC bench said the provisions of the Act could lead to detention of the accused without trial for long, which is akin to a statute enjoining preventive detention, and there is no safeguard against such preventive detention."However compelling the social menace, any penal enactment cannot lead to arbitrary actions. A mere allegation can trigger a gang chart, arrest and year-long remand. There is no safeguard against vindictive and malicious action against 'the innocent, the righteous, the virtuous, a whistleblower'," it said.
Article Summary: Sc flags ‘serious flaws’ in up gangsters act, warns of misuse against innocents. Justices j b pardiwala and k vinod chandran said the special act does not create any offence, which is the requirement of any penal law.

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Friday hit back at the Congress after several of its leaders paid tribute to former party leader Sajjan Kumar, a convict in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, who died at 80 Congress MP Deepender Hooda described the death of Kumar, a former three-term Lok Sabha MP, as an "irreparable loss.""Today, the country's political landscape has suffered an irreparable loss... Sajjan Kumar ji was a leader whose connection with people in Delhi and across north India was cited as a model across the country," he said.Reacting to Hooda's remarks, BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress of "eulogising the killers of the Sikh community", referring to Kumar's role in the anti-Sikh riots."Congress calls late Sajjan Kumar, a man convicted in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, a 'role model'! How can Congress eulogise the killers of our Sikh community?" Bhandari posted on X."This is the real mindset of 'Mohabbat Ki Dukkan' (shop of love) of Rahul Gandhi and exposes the innate hate Congress has for the Sikh community!" Bhandari added, referring to a phrase used by Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha.The BJP spokesperson further demanded that Congress apologise for "insulting" the victims of the anti-Sikh riots and "rubbing" salt into the wounds of the survivors and victims' families.Congress leader Udit Raj also described Kumar's death as a "great loss" for the party."It is a great loss for the Congress. He was a very senior Congress leader, and it will be difficult to fill the void... He did a lot of work, especially for the poor," Raj stated.Sajjan Kumar died at Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital on Thursday."Sajjan Kumar was brought to Safdarjung Hospital by police with altered sensorium around 11 am. He was immediately admitted and resuscitation measures were initiated. Despite providing all necessary medical and life-support measures, he could not be saved and passed away at 12:30 pm," the hospital's statement read."He was a known case of high blood pressure and Parkinson's disease and had a history of multiple hospital admissions in the past," the statement added.Kumar was serving multiple life sentences after his conviction in cases linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi.He was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Delhi High Court on December 17, 2018, in a case related to the killing of five Sikhs and the burning of a gurdwara during the anti-Sikh riots.He was also sentenced to life imprisonment by a Delhi court in February 2025 in another case relating to the killing of two Sikh men during the riots.Kumar resigned from the primary membership of the Congress after the 2018 conviction.

Article Title: India, Nepal to drone-map 'Dasgaja' encroachments after Balen remark row
Article Text:
(Representative image) The decision was taken at the 13th meeting of the Survey Officials Committee, led by deputy chiefs of Nepal’s Survey Department and Survey of India, in Lucknow last week (Photo: ANI)

NEW DELHI: India and Nepal have decided to use drones to map encroachments along 'Dasgaja' areas — the 10-yard no-man’s strip along the international boundary. The two countries will also look at “cross-border occupation”, where citizens of one nation farm, live on or hold land falling on the other side, across the 1,880km open border.The decision was taken at the 13th meeting of Survey Officials Committee, led by deputy chiefs of Nepal’s Survey Department and Survey of India, in Lucknow last week. Officials said the exercise will create a jointly verified technical record of affected areas, which can later help the two countries negotiate removal of encroachments, restoration of land or compensation.The issue returned to Nepal’s political centre stage after PM Balendra Shah told Parliament in May that "Nepal had also encroached on Indian land". The remark came when Shah was questioned about Limpiyadhura, Lipulekh and Kalapani — territories under India which Nepal claims as its own — and triggered opposition protests. Nepal’s foreign ministry later clarified that Shah was referring to Dasgaja encroachments and cross-border occupation, not territorial claims.Nepal Survey Department spokesperson Dayanand Joshi said, “It has been decided to map cross-border occupation using drones.”He added, “This includes cross-border occupation and also encroachment of Dasgaja.”Border expert and former Survey Department director general Buddhi Narayan Shrestha said the decision could help settle disputes that have lingered for decades. “Indian farmers have encroached on the land of Nepali farmers along the border, and Nepali farmers have also encroached on the land of Indian farmers to some extent. I call this cross-border land grabbing,” he said.Shrestha said his 2005 field study found Indian farmers occupying Nepali land at 84 locations and Nepali farmers occupying Indian land at 27 locations. He said such disputes arose where boundary pillars were missing or mistakes were made during local land use. “It will take some time for technicians from Nepal and India to compile such a list,” Shrestha said. “Once the data is in hand, the decision on how to resolve the issue should be made through negotiations by higher-level officials sitting at the table.Shrestha cited Nepal’s past border demarcation with China, where local officials from Tibet and Nepal resolved similar disputes through sale windows and compensation. He said nearly 42 per cent of the 8,553 border pillars shown on maps are yet to be installed, making drone mapping crucial for preventing village-level disputes from turning into diplomatic flashpoints.
Article Summary: India and nepal have decided to use drones to map encroachments along 'dasgaja' areas. The two countries will also look at “cross-border occupation’ across the 1,880km open border. Officials said the exercise will create a jointly verified technical record of affected areas.

Article Title: 'You don't belong to anyone else, but yourself': Rahul Gandhi's message to young women
Article Text:

What is ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ about?

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday described India’s 70 crore women as the country’s “biggest asset”, saying they are more forward-looking than men and have a crucial role in shaping the nation’s future. He also invoked the idea of women's autonomy and said that a woman should have the exclusive ownership of her own life.Speaking at the fourth event of 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' at the AISSMS College Ground in Pune, Maharashtra, he invoked a verse from the Manusmriti and contrasted it with his call for the empowerment and autonomy of women.Rejecting the idea of women being liable to other men, he asserted that a woman's exclusive ownership belongs to herself. While acknowledging that the relationships in a woman’s life are important, he stressed that they do not determine her identity or ownership.Speaking on the central theme of the evening, “break the cage”, Rahul Gandhi called on the audience to recognise the individuality that sets each person apart and to resist the pressures that seek to confine them to predetermined identities or expectations. He said the most important message he wanted people to take away from the evening was a simple but powerful one: “Every single one of you is unique in this universe.Elaborating on the idea, Rahul Gandhi stressed that individuality is not merely about being different from others, but about recognising one’s own worth and identity. “You are unique. You are special. You are an individual,” he told the audience. He emphasised that every person has a distinct way of looking at the world, a different set of aspirations and the ability to imagine a life beyond the boundaries imposed on them.Rahul further connected this sense of individuality to the freedom to dream and choose one’s own path. “And you have your own dream, your own vision for your life,” he said. The emphasis, he suggested, was not simply on having dreams, but on having the freedom to define those dreams for oneself rather than allowing society, circumstances or established notions of what one ‘should’ be to determine them.Through the theme of “break the cage”, the LoP framed personal freedom as the ability to step outside these limitations and acknowledge that no individual should be reduced to a role, label or identity prescribed by others. His message was that recognising one’s uniqueness is the first step towards claiming the freedom to shape one’s own future, pursue one’s aspirations and live according to one’s own vision of life.Rahul Gandhi launched a sharp attack on the Manusmriti over its treatment of women, criticising the text’s prescription that women should remain under the authority of male relatives throughout their lives. He contrasted the idea with his call for women’s autonomy, arguing that a woman’s identity and freedom should not be defined by her relationship with her father, husband or sons.Quoting from the Manusmriti, Rahul Gandhi said, “I (would) like to quote here the Manusmriti, which says clearly that in childhood a female must be subject to her father, in youth she belongs to her husband and, when her lord is dead, she belongs to her sons. A woman must never be independent.”Calling the words unacceptable, Rahul Gandhi added, “These words are a shame. These words should not have been spoken.” He said the country should instead recognise women as individuals with their own aspirations and agency, describing India’s 70 crore women as its “biggest strength” because of their “70 crore unique journeys, unique imagination, unique dreams”.His remarks framed the debate around women’s independence as a broader question of individual freedom, with Rahul arguing that women should have the right to define their own identities and determine the course of their lives rather than be treated as belonging to male relatives.The event follows a political storm and clashes between student organisations. The programme was preceded by a midnight clash between the NSUI and ABVP at the COEP Technological University hostel.It happened after ABVP claimed that female students were being forced to attend the event. Meanwhile, Congress leaders countered the claims, saying two female students, who had earlier expressed their support for the event, were threatened and confined inside the hostel.BJP has also accused Congress of paying influencers and manufacturing crowds for the event. Meanwhile, Congress has alleged that the ruling establishment was attempting to disrupt Rahul Gandhi’s student outreach.Tensions escalated on Friday night when NSUI and ABVP members clashed at the COEP hostel campus ahead of the LoP’s interaction. Police resorted to a lathi charge to control the situation, while several injured activists were taken to Sancheti Hospital.According to police sources cited in the material, the Shivajinagar Police registered cases against 50 to 60 people, including six named NSUI and Youth Congress activists, following a complaint by an ABVP member.The confrontation reportedly centred on student participation in LoP Rahul Gandhi’s programme. NSUI activists said they were responding to distress calls from female students, while ABVP alleged that Congress-linked workers were forcibly encouraging hostellers to register for the event.Congress leaders accused ABVP workers of entering the girls’ hostel and intimidating students who had expressed support for the event.Congress spokesperson Atul Londhe alleged that a female student was cornered and forced to apologise on camera. NSUI state president Sagar Salunke claimed that students had called the organisation for help and alleged that CCTV cameras had been switched off before NSUI members arrived.Salunke also alleged that students, including orphaned students, had been pressured to record videos praising the college administration. The case registered by police followed a complaint from 21-year-old student Malhar Nilesh Patil, who alleged that a student’s video statement had been recorded under pressure at the hostel.Congress leader Pawan Khera alleged that there had been a conspiracy to disrupt LoP's Pune programme, claiming that the response among young people had rattled those in power.Khera linked the controversy to the issues female students were expected to raise with Rahul, including alleged diversion of scholarship funds. He accused ABVP workers of intimidating students and said the incident reflected an attempt to keep women away from public decision-making.He also invoked Pune’s history as the city where Savitribai Phule pioneered women’s education, arguing that the theme of the event was particularly relevant to the city.The BJP launched a separate attack on the programme, accusing the Congress of paying influencers to mobilise attendance and promote Rahul Gandhi’s event on social media.BJP Maharashtra spokesperson Navnath Ban alleged that influencers were being offered Rs 30,000 to Rs 35,000 each, along with travel expenses, and claimed that the overall expenditure could reach Rs 9 crore to Rs 10 crore if around 3,000 people were paid.Ban dubbed the programme ‘Paise Ki Goonj’ instead of ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ and demanded an investigation into the source of the alleged funds. BJP leader Keshav Upadhyay separately accused Rahul Gandhi of using student issues as a political platform.The Congress rejected the BJP’s allegations and accused it of trying to create obstacles to LoP Rahul Gandhi’s programme because of his growing support among young people.Maharashtra Congress spokesperson Sachin Sawant claimed that the BJP was particularly apprehensive about Rahul's appeal among Gen Z and alleged that authorities and ABVP members had attempted to disrupt the programme.NCP (SP) leader Mahesh Tapase also criticised the BJP, saying there was no reason to oppose a programme focused on issues affecting students and young people.Rahul’s Pune interaction with female students is centred on student and youth concerns, with issues such as paper leaks, unemployment and the education system expected to feature in the programme.The Congress has sought to position the initiative as a platform for students to directly raise their concerns, while the BJP has characterised it as a political campaign by the Leader of the Opposition. The Pune event, therefore, has begun against the backdrop of an escalating political battle over who controls the narrative around student and youth concerns.
Article Summary: Rejecting the idea of'manusmriti', he asserted that a woman belongs to no one but herself. Rahul gandhi calls on the audience to recognise the individuality that sets each person apart and to resist the pressures that seek to confine them to predetermined identities.

Article Title: 20 Blackbucks rewilded in Banni Grasslands on India’s 80th Independence Day by Anant Ambani’s Vantara
Article Text:
Part of a wider Gujarat Native Herbivore Conservation Programme

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

On India’s 80th Independence Day, the Gujarat Forest Department, with technical support from Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre (GZRRC), Vantara, released 20 blackbucks also known as antilope cervicapra, into the Banni Grasslands of Kutch, marking an important milestone in the restoration of native wildlife and the ecological character of this unique grassland landscape.The release comprised five male and 15 female blackbucks, transferred from Vantara, Jamnagar, following the requisite approvals of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, and the Central Zoo Authority (CZA). The transfer was undertaken in accordance with prescribed protocols covering veterinary examination, health screening, quarantine, disease surveillance, safe and humane transportation and release. Vantara complied with all the necessary requirements.The significance of the initiative extends beyond the release of 20 animals. Restoring native herbivores is an important part of rebuilding the ecological fabric of Banni, strengthening its native herbivore community, supporting natural predator prey relationships and contributing to the recovery of a more resilient grassland ecosystem.Banni is a vast grassland landscape supporting pastoral communities and diverse native wildlife. Blackbuck, chinkara, nilgai and wild boar have historically formed part of its herbivore assemblage. Their recovery, alongside habitat conservation and scientific grassland management, can help restore the ecological character and biodiversity of the landscape.The initiative reflects the broader national commitment to the revival of India’s native species and restoration of its grassland ecosystems, a conservation direction strongly championed under the leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi.Dr Jaipal Singh, IFS, Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, said, “Restoring native wildlife is fundamental to restoring healthy landscapes. The release of these 20 blackbucks into Banni on India’s Independence Day is an important milestone in our continuing effort to recover the ecological character and biodiversity of this unique grasslands. Such restoration requires science, sustained management and collaboration, and we appreciate Vantara’s technical support in carrying out the programme in accordance with prescribed protocols. ”Ajit Kulkarni, Special Director, Compliance & Due Diligence, Vantara, said, “There can be no greater privilege on Independence Day than contributing to a future in which India’s native species continue to live and flourish in the natural landscapes to which they belong. Species restoration is not simply about releasing animals; it requires a thorough understanding of the habitat, the species and the individual animals being released, as well as habitat dynamics, population planning, and the active support of all stakeholders, particularly local communities, to ensure the long term success and sustainability of these efforts. We are honoured to support the Gujarat Forest Department and the Government’s conservation vision for Banni, and to contribute our technical capabilities wherever they can strengthen India’s wildlife conservation efforts.”The Banni release forms part of a wider programme to strengthen native herbivore populations across Gujarat. The Central Government, through the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, has approved the translocation of 500 blackbucks and 100 chinkara, with the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, providing the necessary directions for the exercise.While components of this wider programme support prey base augmentation in connection with the planned cheetah reintroduction programme, the Banni blackbuck release also has an important and independent species restoration objective: rebuilding populations of wildlife native to the grasslands.The Banni Grassland Forest Division has sought Vantara’s technical support for the wider translocation programme, including specialised herbivore transport vehicles, portable boma systems, veterinary expertise and technical support for safe handling and transportation.The initiative builds on the Gujarat Forest Department’s sustained conservation work. With the approval of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, Vantara has previously supported the Forest Department in the rewilding of nearly 80 spotted deer in Barda Wildlife Sanctuary, contributing to biodiversity strengthening within the Asiatic lion conservation landscape.
Article Summary: 20 blackbucks released into banni grasslands of kutch on india's 80th independence day. Part of a wider gujarat native herbivore conservation programme to strengthen native herbivore populations. Vantara complied with all the necessary requirements to release the animals.

NEW DELHI: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday unveiled a structural overhaul of its organisation following its defeat in the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections in April, when it lost power after a single term.DMK’s executive committee, headed by party supremo and former chief minister MK Stalin , met at Anna Arivalayam, the party’s state headquarters in Chennai, and passed nine key resolutions aimed at radically restructuring the organisation.Addressing the meeting, Stalin acknowleded that the changes would be "stringent" and even "difficult" for some to accept."The functioning of our party office-bearers is also one of the reasons for our defeat. We must first acknowledge our mistakes. We are going to make several changes in the party’s organisational structure. They will certainly be stringent, and for some, they may even be difficult to accept,” the former chief minister said.“Going forward, we are going to introduce age limits and terms of office for various organisational posts, according to the responsibilities involved. We are going to give a larger number of organisational responsibilities to newcomers.We can regain political success only by restructuring the party. We must carry out the organisational reforms as quickly as possible,” he added.Under the new blueprint, the DMK leadership has introduced strict age limits, a mandatory two-term cap for all posts and a major expansion of organisational districts, with the aim of professionalising party operations and facilitating generational succession.The DMK will increase the number of organisational districts from 78 to 110, with each district broadly covering two assembly constituencies to ensure more localised administration. Once Stalin formally releases the boundary maps for the 110 revamped districts, district executive committees will have to convene within 15 days under the supervision of the party headquarters to implement the transition.The standalone post of “city secretary” in major urban centres such as Coimbatore and Tambaram has also been abolished. Instead, urban zones will be redrawn based on voter density, with Chennai Corporation Area Committees averaging 40,000 voters and those in other corporations averaging 30,000 voters per committee.Following Stalin’s defeat in his Kolathur Assembly constituency in Chennai, the DMK is now being led in the Tamil Nadu assembly by his son and former deputy chief minister Udhayanidhi Stalin, who is now serving as the leader of the opposition.

Article Title: Of funds from 19 common donors in 2024, BJP got nearly four times as much as Congress
Article Text:
AI image for representation

Business money dominates

How the number was tallied

Five donors did the heavy lifting

How commons donors contributed to two major parties

Two companies, a perfect 50:50 split

Not just BJP and Congress

How donors contributed to multiple parties

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The 2024 Lok Sabha election results came as a surprise to many politicians and seasoned poll watchers alike. BJP , which had won clear majorities in 2014 and 2019, finished with 240 seats, 32 short of the halfway mark. Narendra Modi needed the support of NDA partners to form a government for a third term.When it came to political donations, however, BJP was the clear leader. India’s national parties declared ₹6,648.56 crore from 11,343 contributions above ₹20,000 in FY2024-25, according to an analysis by the Association for Democratic Reforms, or ADR. That was an increase of ₹4,104.29 crore, or 161%, over the previous financial year.BJP declared ₹6,074.02 crore from 5,522 contributions, up 171% from ₹2,243.95 crore a year earlier. Congress reported ₹517.39 crore from 2,501 contributions, an increase of 84% from ₹281.48 crore. AAP declared ₹38.11 crore, CPI(M) ₹16.96 crore and the National People’s Party ₹2.09 crore. BSP said it had received no donations above ₹20,000.Together, BJP and Congress accounted for 99.14% of the money declared by the six national parties covered by ADR. But buried inside that torrent of money was a curious crossover episode.A TOI examination of the signed FY2024-25 contribution reports submitted by BJP and Congress to the Election Commission has identified at least 19 direct donors whose Permanent Account Numbers, or PANs, appear in both filings.Together, these donors gave at least ₹258.73 crore to the two parties.The money was not divided evenly. BJP received ₹206.64 crore, or 79.87%, while Congress received ₹52.09 crore, or 20.13%. In simpler terms, of every ₹5 contributed by these common donors, roughly ₹4 went to BJP. However, the 19 donors accounted for only about 3.4% of BJP’s total declared contributions, while the corresponding figure for Congress was 10.1%.ADR classified ₹6,128.79 crore, or 92.18% of the contributions received by national parties, as coming from corporate or business sectors. Such contributions formed 94.13% of BJP’s declared total and 74.19% of Congress’s.The classification is broader than incorporated companies. It covers the corporate and business categories created by ADR from descriptions in the party filings. The biggest channel for political money was electoral trusts.ADR found that four trusts, Prudent, Progressive, AB General and New Democratic, gave national parties a combined ₹4,024.43 crore, equivalent to 60.53% of the contributions covered by its report. Prudent Electoral Trust alone gave ₹2,180.71 crore to BJP, ₹216.34 crore to Congress and ₹16.42 crore to AAP.These trust flows have been excluded from TOI’s common-donor calculation. An electoral trust pools contributions before distributing money to parties. Unless the records explicitly establish the link, a company contributing to a multi-donor trust cannot be described as having directly funded a particular party.This analysis therefore deals only with donors appearing directly in party contribution reports.TOI counted a donor as common primarily when the same PAN appeared in both filings, with the name and address used as additional checks. Where the name and PAN did not line up clearly, the amount was left out. Similar company names, group relationships or common addresses were not considered sufficient.ADR found 205 contributions worth ₹3.47 crore without declared PAN details across national parties, besides 33 contributions worth ₹38.8 lakh carrying missing or incorrect PAN information.ADR also found that BJP and Congress had not declared payment dates for their contributions. The filings establish that the money was received during FY2024-25, but do not allow every contribution to be placed precisely on the election calendar.The five largest common donors gave ₹208.5 crore, accounting for 80.59% of the ₹258.73-crore pool. The biggest was Derive Investments, a Mumbai-based investment firm. Its PAN appears against four BJP contributions adding up to ₹53 crore. Congress received another ₹5 crore from the same PAN.Next came ITC Infotech India Ltd, ITC’s wholly owned technology and digital-services subsidiary. It gave ₹33.5 crore to BJP and ₹11.5 crore to Congress, or ₹45 crore in all.ITC Ltd, the diversified conglomerate with businesses spanning FMCG, cigarettes, paperboards, packaging and agribusiness, gave another ₹39 crore to BJP and ₹4 crore to Congress. Its two-party total was ₹43 crore. ITC Ltd and ITC Infotech have been counted separately because they are separate legal entities carrying separate PANs.The fourth-largest common donor was an individual.Suresh Amritlal Kotak, a veteran cotton trader and industry figure often described by his peers as the “Cotton Man of India”, gave ₹30 crore to BJP and ₹7.5 crore to Congress, or ₹37.5 crore in all.Then came Hindustan Zinc Ltd, a Vedanta Group company and integrated producer of zinc, lead and silver. It gave ₹15 crore to BJP and ₹10 crore to Congress.Most large common donors leaned heavily towards BJP. Two companies followed a strikingly different script.Century Plyboards (India) Ltd, the Kolkata-headquartered maker of plywood, laminates and other wood products, gave ₹5 crore to BJP and ₹5 crore to Congress. Star Cement Ltd, a cement manufacturer with plants in Meghalaya, Assam and West Bengal, gave ₹3 crore to each.Micro Labs Ltd, the Bengaluru-based pharmaceutical company best known for the Dolo brand, came close to an even split, giving ₹2 crore to BJP and ₹2.05 crore to Congress.Others leaned sharply towards one party.Finolex Industries, a manufacturer of PVC pipes, fittings and resin, gave ₹5 crore to BJP and ₹1 crore to Congress. Mysore Projects gave ₹3.26 crore to BJP and ₹25 lakh to Congress.Malabar Gold Ltd, the jewellery company subsequently renamed Malabar Gold and Diamonds Ltd, gave at least ₹10.0525 crore to BJP and ₹25 lakh to Congress.Christy Friedgram Industry gave ₹1.90 crore to BJP and ₹1 crore to Congress. The other verified common donors were Russell Credit, Peoples Education Society, Sri City, Muthoot Finance, T V Mohandas Pai, Josco Fashion Jewellers and H S Purewal.Tiger Associates, a West Bengal partnership that describes itself as an area distributor for Nagaland, Sikkim and Punjab state lotteries, gave ₹60 crore to AIADMK, ₹50 crore to DMK and ₹50 crore to Trinamool Congress using the same PAN.That is ₹160 crore across three parties. Of this, ₹110 crore went to the two principal Tamil Nadu rivals, AIADMK and DMK.NATCO Pharma Ltd, a Hyderabad-headquartered pharmaceutical company focused on complex generic medicines and niche molecules, appears across five party filings.Its identified contributions total ₹35.55 crore: ₹16.5 crore to BJP, ₹10 crore to YSR Congress, ₹7 crore to TDP, ₹1.5 crore to Janasena and ₹55 lakh to CPI(M).Century Plyboards also gave ₹1 crore to YSR Congress and ₹50 lakh to TDP, taking its identified contribution across four parties to ₹11.5 crore.Vedanta Ltd, a diversified natural-resources company with operations spanning zinc, aluminium, iron ore, oil and gas, steel and power, identified political contributions of ₹67 crore to BJP, ₹25 crore to BJD and ₹20 crore to JMM in its audited standalone FY2024-25 financial statements. That was ₹112 crore across the three parties. Its broader standalone donation-expense line was ₹116 crore.Not every multi-party combination represents political rivals. BJP, TDP and Janasena contested the 2024 elections in Andhra Pradesh as NDA allies. TDP and YSR Congress, however, fought on opposite sides.Likewise, DMK and AIADMK were direct rivals in Tamil Nadu. BJP and BJD contested against each other in Odisha, while BJP and the JMM-led alliance were the principal opposing camps in Jharkhand.Deng Xiaoping famously said it did not matter whether a cat was black or white, so long as it caught mice. India’s donation filings offer their own lesson in pragmatism. For at least 19 donors, choosing between saffron and Congress blue was apparently not an either-or proposition.
Article Summary: Bjp and congress accounted for 99.14% of the money declared by the six national parties covered by adr. The biggest channel for political money was electoral trusts. At least 19 direct donors whose permanent account numbers, or pans, appear in both filings. Adr found 205 contributions worth ₹3.47 crore without declared pan details across national parties.
